title: One of Google’s Android partners turned 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet
summary: Google partner turns 1.3 million Android set-top boxes into a hidden botnet
detailed: Google announced it has cut ties with Android manufacturing partner Videostrong Technology Co. after discovering an intentional backdoor installed in 1.3 million devices.
The compromised hardware, mostly Android TV set-top boxes and IoT devices, was turned into a botnet used for ad fraud, data exfiltration, and unauthorized network traffic.
Google disrupted the command and control domains associated with the affiliate modules to sever access to additional compromised devices.
sentences: Google says a manufacturer ‘intentionally’ hijacked its devices with malware.

Google says one of its Android manufacturing partners secretly built a backdoor in 1.3 million devices and turned them into a botnet.

The company says it has now dismantled the backdoor and “cut ties” with the manufacturer, the Shenzhen, China-based Videostrong Technology Co., which has been banned from building or selling certified Android devices or supplying software for them.
The infected devices were used without owners’ knowledge for “malicious activity,” like ad fraud, data exfiltration, and routing unauthorized network traffic.

Google claims the “backdoor and botnet were intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial gain,” saying:
Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices.
These secondary modules were conducting ad-fraud; silently enrolling infected devices into residential proxy networks; and loading additional malware onto XCPE-compromised devices.
We also took action to disrupt the command and control (C2) domains that operate these affiliate modules.

Because these affiliates each have diversified distribution channels for their modules beyond XCPE, we assess that taking down their C2 domains will sever access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices.
Google also says it made changes to its review process for device manufacturers after this incident.
